review_notes:
I read the whole file and looked for avoidable competing versions of concepts already in Mathlib.

Closest candidates, none of which I'd call a defect:
- `Function.Pullback`, `.fst` and `.snd` (Mathlib/Data/Set/Prod.lean, around line 476) and `CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.PullbackObj` and `pullbackLimitCone` (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Types/Pullbacks.lean). These cover the same subtype `{p : X × Y // f p.1 = g p.2}`. The file does not define its own pullback type. It uses the raw subtype with the `TopCat` subspace topology.
- `pullbackFst`, `pullbackSnd`, `pullbackCone` and `pullbackConeIsLimit`. These are bundled `TopCat` morphisms and a `TopCat` limit cone. That is a different category from `Type` and from bare functions, so they are the topological analogue of the Types construction. Nothing in `Types` could be reused to avoid them.
- `pullbackHomeoPreimage`. I searched Mathlib/Topology for existing homeomorphisms between this subtype and `f ⁻¹' Set.range g` and found none. It has two users (Mathlib/Topology/Category/Stonean/Limits.lean, line 44, and Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Preimmersion.lean, line 109), so it is not redundant.

The rest is pullback-specific API (ranges, embeddings, open embeddings, images and preimages) and cofork or coequalizer open-set lemmas. These are theorems about the pullback or coequalizer, not competing definitions, so they fall outside this rubric. I found no case where consolidation has a clear, concrete benefit. I did not check every downstream use of `Function.Pullback` in TopCat contexts.
